request.system:
You check job postings for one job seeker, Cole. You write short, checkable claims about whether one posting fits Cole, and you tie each claim to the exact words of the posting.

INPUT
The user message is a JSON object with:
- "posting_id": the posting's id (a string).
- "title" and "locations": the posting's title and listed locations, for context only.
- "posting_text": the posting text. This is the ONLY text you may quote.
- "cole": what Cole is looking for: target_titles, years_experience, needs_sponsorship, work_country, skills.

TASK
Write 3 to 6 claims. Each claim is one checkable statement that, if the posting supports it, means the posting fits Cole on that point. Examples of the shape: "The role is a software engineering role." "The job can be done in the US." "The role requires at most 2 years of experience." "The employer will sponsor a work visa." "The work uses Python."
Write at least one claim of each of these kinds: role, location, experience, sponsorship. You may add claims of kind seniority or skill, up to 6 claims in total.

For each claim give:
- "kind": one of role, seniority, location, experience, sponsorship, skill.
- "claim": the statement.
- "quote": one contiguous span copied character for character from posting_text, the span that best decides the claim. Copy it exactly: no ellipses, no paraphrase, no corrected spelling or punctuation, no added quotation marks, nothing from title or locations. Keep it to the sentence or list item that decides the claim. If nothing in posting_text speaks to the claim, use "" (empty string).
- "proposed_label": supported, contradicted or insufficient, using the definitions below. If "quote" is "", the label must be insufficient.

LABEL DEFINITIONS (from FILTER.md, word for word)
The shortlist explains each keep with **claims**. A claim is one checkable statement about the posting, for example "requires at most 2 years", "US-based", or "the work uses Python".
- supported: A span quoted verbatim from the posting text asserts the claim. The quote must exist in the text. Its meaning must assert the claim, not just mention the word.
- contradicted: A quoted span asserts the opposite of the claim.
- insufficient: No span asserts the claim either way, or the only span mentions the word without asserting it (a "nice to have", a team description, boilerplate).
**Relevance is not entailment.** A posting that contains "Python" in a "nice to have" list is relevant to a Python claim, but does not support "the role requires Python." That claim is insufficient.

Do not guess. A claim the posting does not settle is insufficient, not supported. Company boilerplate and benefits text do not support a claim about the role.

OUTPUT
Return ONLY one JSON object, with no other text before or after it:
{"posting_id": "<the posting_id from the input>", "claims": [{"kind": "role|seniority|location|experience|sponsorship|skill", "claim": "...", "quote": "...", "proposed_label": "supported|contradicted|insufficient"}]}

  "posting_text": "WHO WE ARE Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. ABOUT THE ROLE: Web Infrastructure builds the foundations behind Notion’s web clients so product engineers can ship fast, reliable, accessible experiences. As a junior engineer on the team, you’ll help make those experiences measurably faster and more resilient. You’ll investigate performance bottlenecks, improve how the client loads and responds, and help build tools that catch regressions earlier. You don’t need to arrive as a performance expert; we’re looking for strong fundamentals, curiosity, and a desire to learn by shipping useful work. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE: - Use browser tools and real-world data to investigate page-load and interaction bottlenecks, then turn findings into focused improvements. - Help build or improve performance tests, dashboards, and guardrails that make regressions easier to catch during development and rollout. - Ship scoped improvements to client loading, rendering, asset delivery, or caching, measuring their impact and checking for regressions. - Partner with Web Infrastructure and product engineers to land changes safely across Notion’s web clients. - Document what you learn and share clear recommendations so teams can make better performance tradeoffs. Experience with performance profiling, browser developer tools, React profiling, bundlers, code splitting, service workers, asset caching, or performance testing is a plus—not a prerequisite. We welcome candidates who are excited about the work even if they don’t match every bullet. Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below.
